The district covers an area of {{cvt|4003|km2}}.{{cite web |title=District Gonda, Government of Uttar Pradesh |url=https://gonda.nic.in/ |website=Official Website of Gonda District Administration |publisher=Government of Uttar Pradesh |access-date=3 October 2025}} {{Pie chart |caption = District-wide vote share by party in Gonda (Assembly elections, 2022). Accessed 3 October 2025. |label1 = [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] |value1 = 51.70 |color1 = #ff9933 |label2 = [[Samajwadi Party|SP]] |value2 = 37.31 |color2 = #ff0000 |label3 = [[Bahujan Samaj Party|BSP]] |value3 = 4.25 |color3 = #0000ff |label4 = [[Indian National Congress|INC]] |value4 = 3.56 |color4 = #00ccff |label5 = Others (incl. smaller parties, independents & NOTA) |value5 = 3.19 |color5 = #aaaaaa |width=100% }} == History == === Early / Ancient period === The area of present-day Gonda district lay within the ancient kingdom of [[Kosala]], one of the sixteen [[Mahajanapadas]] of early India, with [[Ayodhya]] and [[Shravasti]] as major centres.{{cite web |title=Kosala |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Kosala |website=Encyclopaedia Britannica |access-date=3 October 2025}}{{cite book |last=Thapar |first=Romila |title=Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300 |publisher=University of California Press |year=2004 |isbn=978-0-520-24225-8 |pages=131–133}} Archaeological remains associated with early Buddhism have been discovered in the region, particularly around Shravasti.{{cite book |last=Nevill |first=H. R. |title=Gonda: A Gazetteer, Being Volume XLIV of the District Gazetteers of the United Provinces of Agra and Oudh |publisher=Government Press |location=Allahabad |year=1905 |pages=115–116, 149–150, 156–157 |url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.48072 |access-date=19 April 2021}}{{cite web |url=http://www.indiadivine.org/audarya/hinduism-forum/172928-excavations-sravasti.html |title=Excavations at Sravasti |website=IndiaDivine.org |date=June 2002}}{{unreliable source?|date=October 2025}} === Medieval and early modern period === In the early medieval era, the region was ruled by the [[Kalachuris of Sarayupara]] (c. 8th–11th centuries), whose domain along the Sarayu (Ghaghara) included parts of Bahraich and Gonda.{{cite web |title=Indian dynasty of Sarayupara (8th–11th century) |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kalachuri-Dynasty-Indian-dynasty-of-Sarayupara-8th-11th-century |website=Encyclopaedia Britannica |access-date=3 October 2025}} From the 12th century onward, Gonda was gradually absorbed into larger north Indian polities and became part of the administrative apparatus of the [[Awadh]] region under successive sultanates and later the [[Mughal Empire]].{{cite web |title=Awadh |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Awadh |website=Encyclopaedia Britannica |access-date=3 October 2025}} === Company and British period === Gonda was originally part of the [[Nizamat]] of [[Gorakhpur]]. After the cession of Gorakhpur to the British in 1801 under a treaty with the Nawab of Oudh, Gonda was united administratively with [[Bahraich district|Bahraich]].{{cite book |last=Basu |first=Purnendu |title=Oudh and the East India Company, 1785–1801 |publisher=Maxwell Company |location=Lucknow |year=1943}} When Awadh was annexed in 1856 by the British, Gonda was constituted as a separate district.{{cite web |title=District Census Handbook: Gonda (2011), Part A |url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/1218/download/3886/DH_2001_0952_PART_A_DCHB_GONDA.pdf |publisher=Directorate of Census Operations, Uttar Pradesh |date=2011 |page=5 |access-date=3 October 2025}} On 7 January 1875, a boundary settlement ceded the tract between '''Baghaura Tal''' and the '''Arrah River''' to [[Nepal]].{{cite book |title=Bahraich: A Gazetteer |publisher=Government Press |year=1903 |pages=83–84 |url=https://ia801402.us.archive.org/26/items/in.ernet.dli.2015.47986/2015.47986.Baharaich---A-Gazetteer_text.pdf |access-date=3 October 2025}} === Swaminarayan's birthplace – Chhapaiya === The village of [[Chhapaiya]] in Gonda district is widely recognized as the birthplace of [[Swaminarayan]] (born Ghanshyam Pande in 1781).{{cite web |title=Shree Swaminarayan Temple Chhapaiya |url=https://gonda.nic.in/tourist-place/shree-swaminarayan-temple-chhapaiya/ |website=District Gonda Official |access-date=3 October 2025}}{{cite web |title=Chhapaiya – Swaminarayan Birth Place |url=https://holyvoyages.com/chhapaiya/about-chhapaiya-swaminarayan-birthplace-gonda-uttar-pradesh-india.aspx |access-date=3 October 2025}} This is an established fact in local government and pilgrimage sources, though academic historical research on the early life of Swaminarayan is limited. === Role in the Indian independence movement === Gonda was involved in India's struggle for independence. Notably, [[Raja Devi Bakhsh Singh]] escaped to [[Nepal]] during the [[Indian Rebellion of 1857|1857 rebellion]].{{cite book |last=Rag |first=Pankaj |title=1857: The Oral Tradition |publisher=Rupa Publications |year=2010 |isbn=9788129116222}} It is also recorded that [[Chandra Shekhar Azad]] sought refuge in the region, and [[Rajendra Lahiri]] was imprisoned and executed in Gonda Jail.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}{{cite book |last=Balvally |first=Shubhan |title=Arihant Reprogrammed (Part 4): Mission Martyrs |publisher=Notion Press |date=2024 |isbn=9798894463216}} === Recent history === In independent India, the district came into the national spotlight following the [[1982 Gonda Encounter]], in which 13 persons were killed in a staged police encounter. In 2013, a special CBI court sentenced three policemen to death and five others to life imprisonment for their roles in the case.{{cite news |title=3 cops get death, 5 life term for Gonda fake encounter |work=The Pioneer |date=6 April 2013 |url=http://www.dailypioneer.com/nation/3-cops-get-death-5-life-term-for-gonda-fake-encounter.html |access-date=14 March 2022 |archive-date=3 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203041659/http://www.dailypioneer.com/nation/3-cops-get-death-5-life-term-for-gonda-fake-encounter.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite news |last=Rai |first=Rajat |title=3 cops get death penalty, life term to 5 in Uttar Pradesh fake encounter case |work=India Today |date=5 April 2013 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/uttar-pradesh-gonda-fake-encounter-case-cbi-court-policemen-death-penalty-157895-2013-04-05 |access-date=14 March 2022}} == Economy and development == Agriculture and the sugar industry are the mainstays of the economy of Gonda district. Several sugar mills are located in and around the district: * The Balrampur Chini Mills Limited unit at Babhnan is operational. It also hosts a molasses-based distillery, commissioned with a capacity of 60 kL/day in 2004.{{cite web |title=Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd., Babhnan – Operational Status |url=https://www.anekantprakashan.com/sugar-factory/balrampur-chini-mills-ltd-babhnan-uttar-pradesh/383 |website=Anekant Prakashan |access-date=3 October 2025}}{{cite web |title=About Us – Overview |url=https://chini.com/about-us/overview/ |website=Balrampur Chini Mills |access-date=3 October 2025}} * The Balrampur Chini Mills Limited unit at Mankapur is operational.{{cite web |title=Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd., Mankapur – Operational Status |url=https://www.anekantprakashan.com/sugar-factory/balrampur-chini-mills-ltd-unit-mankapur-mankapur-uttar-pradesh/385 |website=Anekant Prakashan |access-date=3 October 2025}} * The Sarju Sahkari Chini Mills Ltd. at Belrayan is also operational.{{cite web |title=Sarjoo Sahkari Chini Mills Ltd., Belrayan – Operational Status |url=https://www.anekantprakashan.com/sugar-factory/sarjoo-sahkari-chini-mills-ltdbelrayan-kheri-up-belrayan-uttar-pradesh/349 |website=Anekant Prakashan |access-date=3 October 2025}} * The Kisan Sahkari Chini Mills Ltd. at Gonda remains of uncertain operational status.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} In addition to sugar processing, alcohol production through molasses-based distilleries contributes to the industrial economy of the district. === Development status === In 2006, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj identified Gonda as one of India's 250 "most backward districts" (out of a total of 640).{{cite web |author=Ministry of Panchayati Raj |date=8 September 2009 |title=A Note on the Backward Regions Grant Fund Programme |publisher=National Institute of Rural Development |url=http://www.nird.org.in/brgf/doc/brgf_BackgroundNote.pdf |access-date=27 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405033402/http://www.nird.org.in/brgf/doc/brgf_BackgroundNote.pdf |archive-date=5 April 2012}} It was also one of 35 districts in Uttar Pradesh that received allocations under the Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF).{{cite web |title=Districts Covered Under BRGF |date=20 July 2022 |publisher=Ministry of Panchayati Raj |url=https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/257/AU398.pdf |access-date=3 October 2025}} The BRGF programme was delinked from the central budget beginning in financial year 2015–16, pursuant to the implementation of the Fourteenth Finance Commission's recommendations of enhanced state revenue share.{{cite web |title=Backward Region Grant Fund (BRGF) |publisher=Press Information Bureau |date=21 December 2021 |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1783879 |access-date=3 October 2025}} Subsequently, Gonda district has been included in the Government of India's Aspirational Districts Programme under the aegis of NITI Aayog, which seeks to accelerate development across health, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, and infrastructure indicators. == Demographics == The total number of literates in the district is 1,679,99 which constitute 48.9% of the total population. Population in the age range of 0 to 6 years was 572,386. The effective literacy (population 7 years and above) was 58.7%. The district has a population density of {{convert|857|PD/sqkm|PD/sqmi}}. Its [[Family planning in India|population growth rate]] over the decade 2001-2011 was 24.17%, higher than the average of Uttar Pradesh (20.09%). Gonda has a [[sex ratio]] of 921 [[Women in India|females]] for every 1000 males, and a sex ratio among children 0–6 years old of 926, both higher than the state average (908 and 899 respectively). 6.55% of the population lives in urban areas. Scheduled Castes made up 15.49% of the population. The human development index of the Gonda district is very low.[http://planningcommission.nic.in/plans/stateplan/sdr_pdf/uphdr_2003e.pdf Planning commission release] === Languages === The official language of the district is [[Hindi]].{{cite web |title=The Uttar Pradesh Official Language Act, 1951 |url=https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/14455?view_type=browse&sam_handle=123456789/1362 |publisher=Government of Uttar Pradesh |access-date=3 October 2025}} At the time of the [[2011 Census of India]], 81.03% of the population in the district reported [[Hindi]] as their mother tongue, 16.04% reported [[Awadhi language|Awadhi]], and 2.68% reported [[Urdu]].{{cite web |title=Table C-16: Population by mother tongue – Uttar Pradesh (District: Gonda) |url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/10224 |website=Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India |publisher=Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India |date=2011 |access-date=3 October 2025}}{{cite web |title=Table C-01: Population by religious community & language – Uttar Pradesh (District: Gonda) |url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/11394 |website=Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India |date=2011 |access-date=3 October 2025}} {{Pie chart |caption = Languages of Gonda district (2011){{efn|Many speakers of Awadhi self-report their mother tongue as "Hindi" in the Census, which leads to Awadhi being underrepresented. See {{cite web |title=Language Census 2011: Concepts & Definitions (C-16) |url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/42458/download/46089/C-16_25062018.pdf |website=Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner |date=2018 |access-date=3 October 2025}} and {{cite book |last=Grierson |first=George A. |title=The Linguistic Survey of India, Volume IX, Part I: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group |publisher=Government of India Press |location=Calcutta |year=1916 |pages=3–15 |url=https://archive.org/details/LSI09 |access-date=3 October 2025}}.}} |label1 = [[Hindi]] |value1 = 81.03 |color1 = orange |label2 = [[Awadhi language|Awadhi]] |value2 = 16.04 |color2 = indianred |label3 = [[Urdu]] |value3 = 2.68 |color3 = green |label4 = Others |value4 = 0.25 |color4 = grey |width=100% }} Awadhi is traditionally the dominant spoken language of the region, as Gonda lies within the cultural area of [[Awadh]].{{cite web |title=Linguistic Survey of India (Vol. XI: Hindi and its mother tongues, incl. Awadhi) |url=https://language.census.gov.in/eLanguageDivision_VirtualPath/LSI_Reports/pdf/11.pdf |publisher=Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India |date=2018 |access-date=3 October 2025}} Although the 2011 Census records over four-fifths of the population as speaking Hindi, this figure includes regional varieties such as Awadhi, which 16.04% explicitly identified. Linguists note that Awadhi continues to be widely used in daily communication, folk songs, oral traditions, and local literature, while standard Hindi serves as the formal and administrative language.{{cite book |last=Masica |first=Colin P. |title=The Indo-Aryan Languages |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1991 |isbn=978-0-521-29944-2 |pages=27–28}} Apart from Hindi, languages spoken in the district include [[Awadhi language|Awadhi]], a variety of the [[Hindi Belt|Hindi continuum]] spoken by over 38 million people in the [[Awadh]] region,{{cite encyclopedia |editor=M. Paul Lewis |encyclopedia=Ethnologue: Languages of the World |title=Awadhi: A language of India |edition=16th |year=2009 |publisher=SIL International |location=Dallas, Texas |url=http://www.ethnologue.com/show_language.asp?code=awa |access-date=3 October 2025}} as well as [[Bhojpuri language|Bhojpuri]] and [[English language in India|English]], though their numbers in the district are too small to be reported separately in the Census. == Tehsils (Sub-district) == There are four [[Tehsil]]s in Gonda district.{{Cite web |title=Tehsil {{!}} District Gonda, Government of Uttar Pradesh {{!}} India |url=https://gonda.nic.in/tehsil/ |access-date=2022-11-27 |language=en-US}} # [[Colonelganj]] # [[Gonda, Uttar Pradesh|Gonda]] # [[Mankapur]] # [[Tarabganj]] == Blocks == Gonda district comprises 16 [[Block (district subdivision)|Blocks]]:{{Cite web |title=Subdivision & Blocks {{!}} District Gonda, Government of Uttar Pradesh {{!}} India |url=https://gonda.nic.in/subdivision-blocks/ |access-date=2022-11-27 |language=en-US}} # Babhanjot # Belsar # Chhapia # Colonelganj # Haldharmau # Itiathok # Jhanjhari # Katra Bazar # Mankapur # Mujehana # Nawabganj # Pandri Kripal # Paraspur # Rupaidih # Tarabganj # Wazirganj == Townships and villages == *[[ITI Township Mankapur]] == Education == The effective [[Literacy in India|literacy rate]] (7+) is 58.71%, the state average (69.72%).[http://www.censusindia.gov.in/2011-prov-results/paper2/data_files/UP/datasheetpaper2.pdf Provisional Population Totals Paper 2 of 2011 - Uttar Pradesh] The government of India has created a special scheme for underdeveloped districts through the "Backward Region Grant Fund". Gonda is one of the recipients of this fund.{{cite web|url=http://www.pib.nic.in/release/release.asp?relid=19785|title=Press information release|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070524035855/http://www.pib.nic.in/release/release.asp?relid=19785 |archive-date=24 May 2007|date=11 August 2006|website=pib.nic.in}} === Institutions and schools === * [[LBS Degree College]] * Meena Shah Institute of Technology and Management (MSITM) Degree College{{Cite web |last=Wahak |first=The Sandesh |date=2021-03-24 |title=गोण्डा : मीना शाह इंस्टिट्यूट ऑफ टेक्नोलॉजी एंड मैनेजमेंट डिग्री कॉलेज में मेधावियों को किया गया सम्मानित |url=https://www.thesandeshwahak.com/gonda-honored-to-meritorious-students-at-meena-shah-institute-of-technology-and-management-degree-college/ |access-date=2023-09-27 |website=The Sandesh Wahak |language=en-US}} * Saraswati Devi Nari Gyansthali P.G. College * St Xaviers Senior Secondary School. * Saraswati Vidya Mandir Inter College Malviya Nagar, Gonda {{Cite web |title=10 Reason Why your child should never attend the St. Xaviers Senior Secondary School, Gonda |url=https://disarrayedfreak.blogspot.com/2024/04/10-reason-why-your-child-should-never.html |access-date=2024-04-11 |website=10 Reason Why your child should never attend the St. Xaviers Senior Secondary School, Gonda}} == Public health == Gonda has 15 hospitals, 27 [[Ayurvedic]] hospitals, 11 [[Homeopathic]] hospitals and 2 [[Unani]] hospitals, in addition to 66 Government Primary Health Centres. Gonda is one of the districts in the list of top 100 districts in order of Infant Mortality Rate in 2011 census data. It also comes in the top 57 districts with the highest maternal mortality rate{{cite web|url=http://www.censusindia.gov.in/2011-common/AHSurvey.html|title=Census of India Website : Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India|website=www.censusindia.gov.in}} Gonda has been listed as cleanest [[Municipal council (India)|Nagar Palika]] in entire Uttar Pradesh according to the Swachhta Sarvekshan 2022 overturning its last position in the country as per the 2017 survey.{{Cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-s-dirtiest-city-gonda-ranks-bottom-in-swachh-bharat-survey-residents-say-it-s-no-surprise/story-OzuD56RlJBiNZjhGjS3fyN.html|title=India's 'dirtiest city' Gonda ranks bottom in Swachh Bharat survey|date=4 May 2017|work=hindustantimes.com|access-date=17 July 2017|language=en}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.jagran.com/uttar-pradesh/gonda-cleanliness-survey-gonda-cleanest-city-in-up-in-cleanliness-ranking-23112726.html|title=Cleanest City: स्‍वच्‍छता रैंक‍िंंग में गोंडा यूपी का सबसे स्‍वच्‍छ शहर, स्वच्छता सर्वेक्षण की रैकिंग जारी|website=Dainik Jagran}} == Notable people == *[[Patanjali]], the Sanskrit author Gonardiya is generally identified with Patanjali, the epithet denotes someone from Gonarda, which has been identified by some with Gonda.Mahamahopadhyaya Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar (1961). extract: Gonda district is an administrative district in the Awadh region of the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. The district headquarters is located at the city of Gonda, which also serves as the administrative centre of the Devipatan division. The district covers an area of 4,003 km2 (1,546 sq mi).
